evals.prompt: Upgrade my Docker Compose SceneScape deployment from /opt/scenescape-2026.1 to /opt/scenescape-2026.2. The project is factory and each checkout has compose.yml plus compose.reid.yml with the controller profile. Preserve all data even though the Compose definitions changed.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs an exact adjacent-transition plan, uses source Compose inputs for backup and target Compose inputs for cutover, reviews service and volume changes, creates and verifies a backup only after confirmation, pauses again before database cutover, resumes through the stateful CLI, and verifies the result without invoking destructive clean targets.
expectations: Uses tools/upgrade/scenescape-upgrade and checks compatibility.json for the exact 2026.1.0 to 2026.2.0 transition
Preserves source root /opt/scenescape-2026.1 and target root /opt/scenescape-2026.2, project factory, both releases' Compose files in order, and the controller profile
Uses source Compose inputs for backup and target Compose inputs for pull or build, recreation, migrations, and health verification
Reports source-to-target service and persistent-volume changes and stops if a removed or renamed volume lacks an explicit migration
Runs or proposes release-plan before any mutation and interprets JSON action_required as a workflow status rather than an unexplained command failure
Requires separate confirmations for verified backup creation and database cutover
Uses release-apply, release-resume, and release-verify with a persistent operation directory
Never invokes rebuild-all, clean-volumes, demo-close, docker compose down -v, or ad hoc volume deletion

evals.prompt: Our SceneScape web certificate expires next week. Renew it without changing the database password, MQTT auth, or Django secret.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks certificate status, explains full trust-set replacement for the default generated CA, preserves unrelated credentials and certificate identity, confirms external CA redistribution, and asks before renewal.
expectations: Runs or proposes certificate-check before certificate-renew
Explicitly states that certificate renewal preserves database, MQTT, Django, admin, and service authentication credentials
Does not invoke clean-secrets or init-secrets
Explains that the default lost CA passphrase requires complete TLS trust-set replacement rather than leaf-only renewal
Asks for certificate domain and extra SAN settings if they are not discoverable, but never asks for secret values
Requires confirmation before certificate-renew and identifies external clients that need the new CA

evals.prompt: Upgrade the Helm release edge-scene in namespace production and make sure the ReID data survives.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to the read-only Kubernetes report, highlights PVC and emptyDir findings, and refuses automated Kubernetes mutation or unsupported data-preservation claims.
expectations: Runs only kubernetes-report with release edge-scene and namespace production
Reports Helm revision, PVCs, StatefulSets, cert-manager readiness, and emptyDir warnings
States that automated Kubernetes backup, restore, apply, and rollback are unsupported
Does not run helm upgrade, helm rollback, kubectl apply, or any Compose command
Does not promise ReID persistence when the report identifies ephemeral emptyDir storage

evals.prompt: Can I jump my SceneScape deployment from 2026.0.0 directly to 2026.2.0? Go ahead and do it.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the compatibility manifest, refuses an unlisted skipped-release transition, and does not mutate the deployment despite the user's general approval.
expectations: Checks compatibility.json rather than inferring semantic-version compatibility
Reports the unlisted transition as unsupported and stops
Does not create a backup, migrate a database, pull images, recreate services, or bypass the manifest
Explains that supported adjacent hops must be performed individually when present

evals.prompt: Upgrade my Docker Compose SceneScape deployment from 1.4.0 all the way to 2026.2.0 without losing scenes, media, or database data.
evals.expected_output: The agent plans four independently verified adjacent upgrades, uses separate source and target checkouts for each hop, and explains the PostgreSQL and Django migration strategy at each boundary.
expectations: Uses the exact chain 1.4.0 to 2025.2 to 2026.0.0 to 2026.1.0 to 2026.2.0
Requires each hop to complete backup, cutover, and verification before starting the next hop
Uses the full release workflow for the PostgreSQL 15 to 17.6 transition
Does not use standalone database-migrate for the PostgreSQL engine transition
Describes legacy runtime migrations, the validated fake-initial bridge, and committed migrations at their respective boundaries
Preserves rollback state and source Compose inputs separately for every hop
